results.question: What is our overall gross profit margin?
results.sql: WITH line_data AS (SELECT ol.unit_price, ol.quantity, ol.line_discount, v.cost FROM order_lines ol JOIN orders o ON ol.order_id = o.order_id JOIN variants v ON ol.variant_id = v.variant_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' AND v.cost IS NOT NULL), totals AS (SELECT SUM((unit_price * quantity - line_discount) / 1.1) AS total_revenue_ex_gst, SUM(cost * quantity) AS total_cost FROM line_data) SELECT ROUND(total_revenue_ex_gst::numeric, 2) AS total_revenue_ex_gst, ROUND(total_cost::numeric, 2) AS total_cost, ROUND(((total_revenue_ex_gst - total_cost) / NULLIF(total_revenue_ex_gst, 0) * 100)::numeric, 2) AS gross_profit_margin_percent FROM totals

results.question: What was our revenue in each of the last 3 months?
results.sql: SELECT date_trunc('month', created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney')::date AS month, ROUND(SUM(total)::numeric, 2) AS revenue FROM orders WHERE financial_status <> 'voided' AND created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney' >= '2026-07-01' AND created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney' < '2026-10-01' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1 ASC;
results.answer: Your revenue for the last three months was $342,251.10 in July, $282,129.97 in August, and $278,068.87 in September. These figures represent the total sales from non-voided orders for each month.
results.assumptions: The 'last 3 months' are defined as July, August, and September 2026, given the data period ends on 2026-09-30. Revenue is defined as the sum of order totals for non-voided orders.

results.question: How did revenue during the EOFY sale (19 June to 5 July 2026) compare to the same number of days immediately before it?
results.sql: WITH periods AS (SELECT 'EOFY' AS period, '2026-06-19'::date AS start_date, '2026-07-05'::date AS end_date UNION ALL SELECT 'Pre-EOFY', '2026-06-02'::date, '2026-06-18'::date), revenue_data AS (SELECT p.period, SUM(o.total) AS total_revenue FROM orders o JOIN periods p ON o.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney' >= p.start_date AND o.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney' < (p.end_date + INTERVAL '1 day') WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY p.period) SELECT period, ROUND(total_revenue::numeric, 2) AS revenue FROM revenue_data ORDER BY period DESC
results.answer: Your revenue increased during the EOFY sale, rising to $246,002.91 compared to $186,171.83 in the 17 days prior. This represents a strong growth in sales during your promotional period. Please note that these figures only include non-voided orders and do not account for potential returns processed after the sale ended.
results.assumptions: The EOFY sale period is defined as 2026-06-19 to 2026-07-05 inclusive (17 days). The comparison period is the 17 days immediately preceding it (2026-06-02 to 2026-06-18). Revenue is defined as the sum of order totals for non-voided orders.

results.question: Which 3 products have sold the fewest units?
results.sql: SELECT p.title, SUM(ol.quantity) AS total_units_sold FROM products p JOIN variants v ON p.product_id = v.product_id JOIN order_lines ol ON v.variant_id = ol.variant_id JOIN orders o ON ol.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY p.product_id, p.title ORDER BY total_units_sold ASC LIMIT 3
results.answer: The three products with the fewest sales are the Rash Vest with 221 units, the Maxi Dress with 232 units, and the Knit Midi Dress with 253 units. Please note that this list only includes items that have sold at least one unit, as products with zero sales were excluded from the data.
results.assumptions: Units sold are calculated as the sum of quantities in non-voided order lines. Products with zero sales are excluded as they do not appear in the order_lines table.

results.question: How many customers have placed 3 or more orders?
results.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS loyal_customer_count FROM (SELECT customer_id FROM orders WHERE customer_id IS NOT NULL AND financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY customer_id HAVING COUNT(order_id) >= 3) AS subquery
results.answer: There are 1,640 customers who have placed three or more orders. Please note that this count is based on unique customer IDs, so it may be higher than the actual number of individuals if some people used multiple accounts.
results.assumptions: Only orders with a non-null customer_id were counted. Voided orders were excluded. The count represents unique customer_id values, which may overstate the number of physical individuals if one person used multiple accounts.

results.question: On average, how many days after the order are refunds issued?
results.sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (r.created_at - o.created_at)) / 86400)::numeric, 2) AS avg_days_to_refund FROM refunds r JOIN orders o ON r.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided'
results.answer: On average, refunds are issued 18.52 days after the original order date. This calculation is based on non-voided orders only and assumes that the refund timestamp accurately reflects when the return process was finalized.
results.assumptions: Calculated the difference between the refund creation timestamp and the original order creation timestamp in days. Only non-voided orders were included.

results.question: How much revenue came from orders that used a discount?
results.sql: SELECT SUM(total) AS revenue_from_discounted_orders FROM orders WHERE financial_status <> 'voided' AND discount_id IS NOT NULL;
results.answer: Your shop generated $944,363.46 in revenue from orders that used a discount between October 2025 and September 2026. This total includes all non-voided orders with a discount applied, assuming that any order missing a discount ID was excluded from the calculation.
results.assumptions: Revenue is defined as the sum of the 'total' column for all non-voided orders that have a non-null 'discount_id'. The data period is 2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30.

results.question: Which colour sold the most units in winter (June to August 2026), and how many?
results.sql: SELECT v.color, SUM(ol.quantity) AS total_units_sold FROM order_lines ol JOIN variants v ON ol.variant_id = v.variant_id JOIN orders o ON ol.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' AND (o.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney') >= '2026-06-01 00:00:00' AND (o.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney') < '2026-09-01 00:00:00' GROUP BY v.color ORDER BY total_units_sold DESC LIMIT 1
results.answer: The Camel colour sold the most units during winter 2026, with a total of 1,050 units sold. This figure is based on non-voided orders recorded between June 1st and August 31st, 2026.
results.assumptions: Winter 2026 is defined as June 1st to August 31st, 2026. Revenue and units are based on non-voided orders. Colour is derived directly from the variants table.

results.question: Compare weekend revenue with weekday revenue.
results.sql: WITH daily_revenue AS (SELECT (created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney')::date AS sale_date, EXTRACT(DOW FROM (created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney')) AS dow, total FROM orders WHERE financial_status <> 'voided'), revenue_by_type AS (SELECT CASE WHEN dow IN (0, 6) THEN 'Weekend' ELSE 'Weekday' END AS day_type, SUM(total) AS total_revenue FROM daily_revenue GROUP BY 1) SELECT day_type, ROUND(total_revenue::numeric, 2) AS total_revenue FROM revenue_by_type ORDER BY day_type DESC;
results.answer: Your weekday revenue was $2,147,980.22, which is significantly higher than your weekend revenue of $1,173,950.49. These figures represent the total sales from October 2025 through September 2026, assuming all orders were correctly categorized by the Sydney timezone.
results.assumptions: Revenue is defined as the sum of order totals for non-voided orders. Weekends are defined as Saturday (6) and Sunday (0) in the Australia/Sydney timezone. Data covers 2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30.

results.question: What is the best-selling product in each product type?
results.sql: WITH product_sales AS (SELECT lower(p.product_type) AS type, p.title, SUM(ol.quantity) AS total_units FROM order_lines ol JOIN variants v ON ol.variant_id = v.variant_id JOIN products p ON v.product_id = p.product_id JOIN orders o ON ol.order_id = o.order_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY 1, 2), ranked_products AS (SELECT type, title, total_units, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY type ORDER BY total_units DESC) as rank FROM product_sales) SELECT type, title, total_units FROM ranked_products WHERE rank = 1 ORDER BY type;
results.answer: The best-selling products are the One-Piece Swimsuit (4,043 units) for swimwear, Straw Hat (3,619 units) for accessories, and Linen Wrap Skirt (1,804 units) for skirts. Other top sellers include the Shirt Dress (1,492), Ribbed Tank (1,395), High-Rise Jeans (1,295), Wool Coat (828), and Merino Crew Jumper (526). These figures represent total units sold between October 2025 and September 2026, excluding any voided orders.
results.assumptions: Best-selling is defined by total units sold across the entire data period (2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30). Voided orders are excluded. Product types are normalized to lowercase as per instructions.

results.question: How many orders contained more than one unit in total?
results.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM (SELECT order_id FROM order_lines JOIN orders USING (order_id) WHERE orders.financial_status <> 'voided' GROUP BY order_id HAVING SUM(quantity) > 1) AS multi_unit_orders
results.answer: There were 8,908 orders that contained more than one unit in total. This figure excludes all voided orders as per your business rules.
results.assumptions: I defined 'more than one unit in total' as the sum of quantities across all line items within a single order being greater than 1. Voided orders were excluded as per the business rules.

results.question: How have sales of the cotton blue dress shirt changed over the last 3 months?
results.sql: WITH monthly_sales AS (SELECT date_trunc('month', o.created_at AT TIME ZONE 'Australia/Sydney') AS sale_month, SUM(ol.unit_price * ol.quantity - ol.line_discount) AS gross_revenue FROM orders o JOIN order_lines ol ON o.order_id = ol.order_id JOIN variants v ON ol.variant_id = v.variant_id JOIN products p ON v.product_id = p.product_id WHERE o.financial_status <> 'voided' AND lower(p.title) ILIKE '%shirt%' AND lower(p.product_type) = 'top' AND o.created_at >= '2026-07-01' AND o.created_at < '2026-10-01' GROUP BY 1) SELECT sale_month, gross_revenue, LAG(gross_revenue) OVER (ORDER BY sale_month) AS previous_month_revenue, (gross_revenue - LAG(gross_revenue) OVER (ORDER BY sale_month)) / NULLIF(LAG(gross_revenue) OVER (ORDER BY sale_month), 0) * 100 AS pct_change FROM monthly_sales ORDER BY sale_month;
results.answer: Sales for shirts decreased overall during the last three months, dropping from $3,892.31 in July to $3,350.34 in September. While revenue remained steady in August, it fell by over 14% in September. Please note that these figures represent all items categorized as shirts, as the store does not stock a specific cotton blue dress shirt.
results.assumptions: The store does not sell a 'cotton blue dress shirt'. I have interpreted this as sales of all items with 'shirt' in the title and 'top' as the product type (e.g., Linen Shirt, Oversized Poplin Shirt). The last 3 months are defined as July, August, and September 2026.
